newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold keeps forecast of higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Ahold keeps forecast of higher profits.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV said on Thursday it maintained its previous forecast that 1996 full-year profits would show a further rise.
The recent acquisition of U.S. retail group Stop & Shop will give a further boost to operating profit and profit after tax, Ahold added.
"Further growth of profits per share is expected to be positively affected by this takeover," the company said in a statement.
Ahold reported its second quarter net profit had risen to 121.3 million guilders, up 18.3 percent from 102.5 million posted in the same period of 1995.
Analysts had expected a second quarter net of between 110.7 million and 123 million guilders.
Ahold said the rise of net profits had been caused by higher operating income in the various geographic areas where it is active. Interest charges and tax had risen, it added.

The net result was further raised by currency gains, in particular because of higher rates for the U.S. dollar. If currency rates had remained unchanged, the second quarter net profit rise would have been limited to 13.8 percent, it said.
Second quarter turnover grew by 15.8 percent to 7.83 billion guilders. Excluding the effects of currency rate changes, sales growth would have been 11 percent, Ahold said.

In the Netherlands, second quarter turnover grew by 6.3 percent to 3.6 billion guilders and sales in the rest of Europe were 27.8 percent higher at 578 million guilders. Turnover of Ahold's U.S. subsidiaries rose by 14 percent to $2.1 billion.
Last month, Ahold said it would restructure its U.S. operations, combining its unit Edwards with Giant Food Stores and Finast with Tops.
"We expect substantial efficiency benefits at relatively short notice from these measures and a rearrangement of market areas," Ahold said.
Stop & Shop, which was acquired last July, will be included in Ahold's figures from the third quarter of this year.
Ahold expects this takeover will considerably boost its turnover, operating income and net profits.

Writing off the goodwill that was paid in the Stop & Shop takeover will affect the group's balance sheet ratios but the effect will be temporary and of an acceptable level, Ahold said without elaborating.
